To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we obtain a model for studying the generalized parton distribution of the nucleon in the momentum space, impact parameter space and transverse position space.
we incorporate perturbative effects in the GPDs calculated in effective light front quark model for nucleon.
we have successfully incorporated the evolution effects in GPDs in light-front quark-diquark model and we have obtained the effective model for the GPDs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of GFDs in light-front model.
the hard gluon evolution of the nucleon GPDs in light-front quark-diquark model.
the evolution of GPsD in the light-front model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the light-front quarks in the nucleon are not free and the gluon field is not static, but the quarks and gluons in the nucleon interact with each other and the gluons are not free.
the light-front quarks in the nucleon, which are evolved by the hard gluons, are the main source of the GPDs.
the light-front quarks in the nucleon can be evolved perturbatively, which is a new result.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the light-front quarks model can be extended to describe the phenomenological G PDs in the transverse impact parameter and the momentum space.
, the evolved GPD can be used to calculate the nucleon observables such as the form factors, parton distributions and the transverse momentum dependent distributions.
the light-front quarks are more appropriate for the study of GPDs in a model-independent manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the light-front model the GPDs are not the Fourier transforms of the impact parameter dependent parton distributions.
the light-front quarks in nucleon are not free but are strongly correlated.
the light-front quarks model can be used as an effective model in the phenomenological study of GPDs.
